summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and a history of amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. He presented with a heart rate of 170, hypoglycemia, and elevated thyroid levels. Management included IV diltiazem for rate control, correction of hypoglycemia and hyperkalemia, and initiation of prednisone and increased methimazole for thyroid storm. He was transitioned to oral diltiazem ER and had stable heart rates by discharge. Peripheral artery disease was diagnosed via ABI testing, and a lidocaine patch was started for leg pain. Hypoglycemia led to temporary discontinuation of Lantus, later restarted at a higher dose. Atorvastatin was held due to myalgias. The patient improved clinically, was discharged home with services, and will follow up with endocrinology, vascular surgery, and nephrology.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
